signals.evidence: Client-side shared-comparison loader trusts an unvalidated network body across the API boundary, inconsistent with the app's own SSR normalizer discipline. ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx:43-47 (frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonUrlHandler.tsx) fetches `${getApiBase()}/api/v1/listings/${id}` and returns `response.json() as Promise<ListingSummary>` — a raw runtime cast with NO shape validation — then pushes each result straight into `addToComparison(listing)` (line 70). The SSR sibling that hits the SAME reality-server listing endpoint deliberately does NOT trust the body: getListing() in app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx:88-89 runs `parseListingDetail(body)` precisely because 'A 200 does not guarantee a well-formed body: an upstream/proxy partial response or a malformed listing is truthy but may be missing required nested fields ... Rendering such a body crashes SSR with a 500.' The client comparison path has no equivalent guard, so a malformed/partial 200 (or a shape mismatch — note the endpoint returns a listing DETAIL body but this code casts it to the narrower `ListingSummary`) is accepted as valid and can crash the client comparison view when a comparison card dereferences a missing nested field (e.g. address/photos). Fix: validate/normalize the fetched body through the same parser family (a `parseListingSummary`/`parseListingDetail`-style guard) before `addToComparison`, dropping bodies that fail the shape check exactly as `Promise.allSettled` already drops rejected ids, instead of the bare `as Promise<ListingSummary>` cast.

Price-map page renders hardcoded Slovak user-facing strings on a multi-language (sk/cs/de/en) public portal, bypassing next-intl. In frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/price-map/page.tsx the property-type filter labels are literal Slovak: `PROPERTY_OPTIONS` (lines 29-34) = 'Všetky' / 'Byty' / 'Domy' / 'Pozemky', rendered verbatim as `{opt.label}` at line 189; and the transaction-type toggle at line 161 is `{tx === 'sale' ? 'Predaj' : 'Prenájom'}`. The rest of the same component is correctly localized via `useTranslations('pages.priceMap')` (line 40), so a de/en/cs visitor to /[locale]/price-map sees the page chrome translated but the sale/rent toggle and all four property-type chips stuck in Slovak. This is a genuine i18n coverage gap (not a design-system TODO): move these labels into the `pages.priceMap` message namespace (messages/{en,sk,cs,de}.json) and render them through `t(...)` keyed by the enum value, matching how the surrounding controls already resolve their text.
